subject.title: [Feature]: Automatic Output Sanitization for Sensitive Data

question: Should automatic sensitive-value sanitization for final user-visible output be a core OpenClaw security feature, a plugin/ClawHub capability built on existing hooks, or out of scope beyond current log/tool/transcript redaction?
rationale: Source inspection proves the gap, but deciding the boundary affects security guarantees, user-visible reply correctness, config compatibility, false-positive policy, and whether plugins may own raw conversation rewriting.

options.title: Define a narrow core sanitizer
options.body: Approve a scoped core design for final-output/tool-output sanitization that reuses current redaction helpers and adds schema, docs, regression tests, and upgrade-safe defaults.

options.title: Route to plugin/ClawHub
options.body: Treat this as an optional sanitizer plugin if current or small new hooks can provide deterministic coverage without adding core policy.

options.title: Limit core to existing redaction
options.body: Document that core redacts logs, transcripts, diagnostics, and tool UI surfaces only, and close or split remaining provider/output masking requests.

recommendation.title: Define a narrow core sanitizer
recommendation.body: Approve a scoped core design for final-output/tool-output sanitization that reuses current redaction helpers and adds schema, docs, regression tests, and upgrade-safe defaults.

likelyOwner.reason: CODEOWNERS makes this group the clearest owner for a new sensitive-output security boundary and any core config/docs it would require.
